html: † I. [כָּר] n.[m.] basket-saddle, בְּכַר־הַגָּמָל Gn 31:34 in the camel-basket, i.e. the basket-saddle of the camel, a sort of palankeen bound upon the saddle proper (cf. Kn in Di and reff.) for basket-saddle read < camel-palankeen; the palankeen, or tent-like erection, on the saddle (BurckhBedouisns and Wahabys, 266 DoughtyArabic Des. i. 437, ii. 304 LaneMod. Egyptians (5) ii. 158 al.), which seems intended here, is distinct from the basket or pannier (in which some women also travelled, Porter Travels ii. 232). ii. כַּר v. in alphabetical order.
